seo.title: Barbershop Loyalty Schemes: Do Stamp Cards Pay? (UK)
seo.description: A free tenth cut costs about 10% of a regular's spend. How to work out whether a barbershop loyalty scheme pays, the UK rules on "free", and a better design.

media.anchor: If the shop is full when the free cut is redeemed, it can also push out a paying client
media.alt: Conditional free haircut costs in a hypothetical barbershop: a paid visit displaced costs about £22; a truly incremental visit in an empty slot costs about £3 in variable expenses
media.caption: Hypothetical example from the article, assuming a £22 cut and approximately £3 variable cost. Actual impact depends on whether a paid booking is displaced
media.rights: Original KERSIVO SVG based on Notion ARTICLE DRAFT v2, no external graphics. The £22 and £3 amounts are alternative counterfactuals, not real performance benchmarks.

media.anchor: Every extra visit the card brings also earns a stamp, so it's worth £16.80 on average
media.alt: Hypothetical barbershop loyalty scheme contribution: ten paid visits yield £190, nine paid visits and one free yield £168; approximately 13.1 percent more total visits are required to break even
media.caption: Illustrative cycle-average economics: ten full-price visits vs nine paid plus one free; around 13.1% more total visits needed to match £190 contribution
media.rights: Original KERSIVO SVG; numbers from Notion ARTICLE DRAFT v2: 10 × £19 = £190, 9 × £22 − 10 × £3 = £168, £190 ÷ £16.80 = 11.31 visits. Assumes averages over full stamp cycles, not a discrete annual forecast.
